description: #184: the test-env be.env used FAKE keys but still pointed OUTBOUND hosts at LIVE providers — LINE_HOST=api.line.me, SMS_8X8_HOST=sms.8x8.com, SUPABASE_PROJECT_URL=dummy.supabase.co, DIFY_API_URL=dify.example.com. An accidentally-invoked otp/sms/line/payment call would then reach the real provider (real SMS send / real charge attempt), even with a fake token — the request still LEAVES. guard.sh scanned only DB hosts, so it declared 'safe' while the outbound pipe was live (same blind-spot class as #177's DB-only scan). Fix (structure, not intent): (1) neutralize every outbound host in be.env to an RFC-2606 `.invalid` domain (DNS-guaranteed non-resolvable) so any accidental call dies at DNS — Omise/SendGrid hardcode their host in the SDK so their fake key is the neutralizer; (2) guard.sh now refuses any REAL provider host (api.line.me|8x8.com|omise.co|api.sendgrid.com|sendgrid.net) found ANYWHERE in an env file (whole-file value scan, comments stripped), fail-closed. Teeth (guard.test.sh, run under bash 3.2, neg-control-first): 18/18 — real 8x8/LINE/omise/sendgrid host → REFUSED, neutralized .invalid → allowed, a comment naming a provider → NOT false-refused; mutant drop a PROVIDER_PATTERN → real host slips → RED. Real-machine: BE booted with the neutralized be.env (Nest 'successfully started', :4000, GET / 200, TypeOrmCoreModule initialized against localhost:5433) and sms.8x8.invalid/line.invalid/dummy.supabase.invalid/dify.invalid all resolve NXDOMAIN while api.line.me still resolves (fail-closed proven WITHOUT firing any otp/payment endpoint). gate_layer=infra/shell + runtime-boot.
